item.title: [SwiftHFR] Notifications: ask for the permission when an account is current, not at launch (#1172)
item.body:
Closes #1172
Claim: cloud/m4q-reliab-opus
Author model: Opus 5.5 (cloud/m4q-reliab-opus)
Reviewer model: Fable 5.2 (cloud/m4q-reliab-opus-review-1172-r1, -r2, -delta; APPROVE on 264c45ca)

**Problem.** At the first launch, iOS's notification prompt appears before any login (`SwiftHFRApp.swift:104-105` → `MPNotificationCenter.prepare()` → `requestAuthorization`). For a logged-out user it means nothing: MP notifications and the badge concern a logged-in account. HIG › Privacy, « Requesting permission »: "Avoid requesting permission at launch unless the data or resource is required for your app to function" and "wait to request permission until people actually use an app feature that requires access".

**Cause.** A port of legacy's launch request (`HFRswift/Swift/HFRswiftApp.swift:27-29` @ `87fe0d1c`, LOT-140).

**Change.**
- At launch, `MPNotificationCenter.registerCategory()` only registers the `mp` category. No prompt.
- `MPNotificationPrompt` asks when an account becomes current, through `AppLifecycle.currentAccountChanged`: a stored account restored at launch, a login, or a switch. This runs once per change, whatever the number of windows.
- It asks only when all of these hold: iOS never asked (`.notDetermined`), and « Notifications » or « Badge messages non lus » is on.
- Logged out, it never asks. After any answer, it never asks again (iOS would not show the prompt anyway).
- Réglages › Notifications MP asks when either switch is turned on: « Notifications » as before (#1060), and « Badge messages non lus » too now (an account can be current while iOS never asked, when both switches were off at the login).
- When an account becomes current, the prompt comes before the account's legacy import step, so it never lands over the import summary.
- `LiveNotificationPermission` is now the only caller of `requestAuthorization(options:)`.
- LOT-140 §Permission and §Tests are updated.

**Tests** (app-hosted; not run here, since Linux cannot build the app):
- `MPNotificationPromptTests`:
  - logged out → no request;
  - an account becoming current → one request, and none for a second account once iOS answered;
  - already allowed, denied or badge-off → none;
  - both switches off → none;
  - the pure rule `asks(account:notifications:badge:authorization:)`;
  - `onlyThePermissionSeamAsksIOS`: red before the change, because `MPNotificationCenter.swift` called `requestAuthorization(options:)`.
- `MPNotificationPermissionTests.turningBadgeOnWhileNeverAsked`: turning the badge on while iOS never asked shows the prompt, with no alert (red on the old `badgeTurnedOn`).
- `MultiWindowTests.theNotificationPromptComesBeforeTheAccountsImportStep`: the whole log of an account change is `ask`, then `importForAccount`.
- `MultiWindowTests.everyWindowSeeingAChangeRunsItsReactionOnce`: the prompt step runs once for the account change. The launch test's exact step list shows the launch never asks. Both are red before the change: `Steps` had no such step.

SwiftLint 0.65.1 `--strict` clean. `ledger.py check-body`: 2 blocks ok.

Device check (#893):
- Fresh install, logged out: no system prompt.
- Log in: the prompt shows once.
- Relaunch: no prompt.
- After a launch whose account restore ran while no window was active, the first activation still shows the prompt, and the account's legacy import step still runs.

### Ledger

```changelog
| UX | Notifications : l'autorisation n'est plus demandée au premier lancement, avant toute connexion, mais quand un compte devient actif (connexion, compte restauré ou changé), une seule fois et seulement si une option de notification ou de pastille est active ; Réglages la demande toujours quand on active les notifications ou la pastille. | LOT-140 #1172 | `HFRswift/Swift/HFRswiftApp.swift:27-29` (`requestNotificationAuthorization` au lancement) @ `87fe0d1c` ; HIG › Privacy, « Requesting permission » |
```

```gap-new
Section: Notifications
| GAP-1172 | Notification permission prompt | Asked at every launch, logged in or not (iOS shows it once). | HFRswiftApp.swift:27-29 @ 87fe0d1c | The `mp` category is registered at launch; the prompt is asked when an account becomes current (restore, login, switch), once, while iOS never asked and « Notifications » or « Badge messages non lus » is on; never logged out; Réglages still asks when « Notifications » or « Badge messages non lus » is turned on. | LOT-140, #1172 | UX change | HIG › Privacy (Requesting permission), #866 review, operator triage 2026-11-19 | b·operator |
```

comments.body:
**Adversarial review (Fable 5.2, cloud/m4q-reliab-opus-review-1172-r1, round 1): REQUEST CHANGES** — head e00a724b

One small blocker (finding 1); the trigger, the wiring and the ledger are otherwise sound.

1. **Low** — `App/SwiftHFR/Notifications/MPNotificationSettingsModel.swift:104-108` and `MPNotificationPrompt.swift:8`. The PR makes `.notDetermined` a lasting state, but `badgeTurnedOn()` never asks: `disagreements` returns `[]` for `.notDetermined`.
   - Scenario: logged out, turn both switches off in Réglages (the section is not gated on an account, `SettingsView.swift:121`); log in (no prompt, by the rule); turn « Badge messages non lus » on. No prompt, no alert, no badge until the next launch's restore.
   - Before this PR the launch request made that state unreachable.
   - The comment at `MPNotificationPrompt.swift:8` says Réglages asks "when a switch is turned on"; only « Notifications » does.
   - Fix: `badgeTurnedOn()` requests when `.notDetermined`, as `notificationsTurnedOn()` does, with a test in `MPNotificationPermissionTests`; correct the comment.

2. **Detail** — `App/SwiftHFR/Root/AppLifecycle.swift:64-65`. The prompt waits for `importForAccount`, so after a login with an incomplete legacy import it comes only when that run ends, possibly over the import summary. Ask first, or say why not.

3. **Detail** — `App/SwiftHFR/Notifications/MPNotificationCenter.swift:5,8`. The header still lists `requestNotificationAuthorization` and "permission" as this type's job; that now lives in `MPNotificationPrompt` / `LiveNotificationPermission`.

4. **Detail, for the #893 device check** — a restore that runs while no window is active calls `requestAuthorization` once, and `isNew` then blocks any retry in that process. Not a regression (the launch `.task` had the same limit). Check that a first activation after such a launch still shows the prompt.

**Verified**
- Run: SwiftLint `--strict` on the changed files, clean. `ledger.py check-body --pr 1254`: 2 blocks ok.
- Read: the legacy citation `HFRswiftApp.swift:27-29` @ 87fe0d1c matches; the "Notifications" GAP section exists and the row has 9 columns.
- Read: `rows` starts empty, so `accounts.current?.id` changes on restore, login and switch. `Steps(` has two call sites, both updated. `requestAuthorization(options:` has one caller, so `onlyThePermissionSeamAsksIOS` was red on the base.
- Read: the `MainActor` and `Sendable` use, the fake actor and the tuple-argument test show no compile error. The foreground badge retries on reactivation after the prompt.
- Reasoned, not run: dropping the step, the account guard, the switch guard or the `.notDetermined` test each turns a test red.
- Not run: the app build and the app tests (Linux).

Round 1 handled in d9b9a6d8:

comments.body:
**Adversarial review (Fable 5.2, cloud/m4q-reliab-opus-review-1172-r2, round 2): APPROVE** — head d9b9a6d8

Round-1 findings: 1 fixed, 2 fixed but untested (finding 2 below), 3 fixed, 4 is a device check for #893. The app cannot be built on Linux, so the Swift was read, not compiled or run.

1. **Low — PR body, `### Ledger` (`changelog` and `gap-new` GAP-1172) and "Change" bullet 5.** Both rows say Réglages asks "when « Notifications » is turned on". Since d9b9a6d8 « Badge messages non lus » asks too (`App/SwiftHFR/Notifications/MPNotificationSettingsModel.swift:106-113`), so the steward would fold an incomplete row. The "Tests" list also omits `turningBadgeOnWhileNeverAsked`. Fix: edit the body ("either switch"); no push needed.

2. **Low — `App/SwiftHFRTests/Root/MultiWindowTests.swift:80-82`.** The prompt-before-import order is not tested: both assertions filter the log, so swapping `App/SwiftHFR/Root/AppLifecycle.swift:65-66` back keeps them green. Fix: assert the order, e.g. `log.entries.prefix(2) == ["ask:a", "importForAccount"]`.

3. **Detail — `App/SwiftHFR/Root/AppLifecycle.swift:65`.** `importForAccount` now waits for the member's answer to the prompt. In practice this is harmless: legacy data to import means the same bundle id (`hfrplus.red.super`), where legacy asked at every launch, so iOS is rarely `.notDetermined`. If `requestAuthorization` did not return while no window is active, the account's import step would not run that launch. Add this to the #893 device check of round-1 item 4.

**Verified**
- Ran: SwiftLint 0.65.1 `--strict` on the whole tree (clean); `ledger.py check-body` on the body ("2 block(s) ok"); `git diff --check`.
- By reading only:
  - `turningBadgeOnWhileNeverAsked` is red on the old `badgeTurnedOn` (0 requests) and green now;
  - the other `MPNotificationPermissionTests` are unaffected, and no other test turns the badge on while `.notDetermined`;
  - nothing in the import (`LegacyImportModel.accountDidChange`, `readStoreAgain`) needs to run before the prompt;
  - `prepare()` has no caller left, and `LiveNotificationPermission` is the only `requestAuthorization(options:)` caller;
  - LOT-140 §Permission, §Réglages and §Tests match the code.

**Adversarial review (Fable 5.2, cloud/m4q-reliab-opus-review-1172-delta, delta pass on 264c45ca)**: APPROVE — head 264c45ca

Scope: `git diff d9b9a6d8 264c45ca` only (one file, +8 lines, `App/SwiftHFRTests/Root/MultiWindowTests.swift:71-77`).

No findings.

Round-2 finding 2 is fixed:
- The new test `theNotificationPromptComesBeforeTheAccountsImportStep` asserts the whole log, unfiltered: `log.entries == ["ask:a", "importForAccount"]`.
- Fails without the change (by reading): swapping `App/SwiftHFR/Root/AppLifecycle.swift:65-66` gives `["importForAccount", "ask:a"]`, so the test goes red.
- No false red on the correct code: `currentAccountChanged` calls only those two steps after its guard, and `Log.steps()` (`MultiWindowTests.swift:231,236`) logs exactly one entry for each. The guard passes on a fresh `AppLifecycle` (`AppWideState.swift:15-19`: nothing seen yet for `currentAccount`). Both steps are awaited in sequence on the main actor with no detached task, so the order is deterministic.
- Swift 6: the test struct and `Log` are both `@MainActor`, the `Steps` closures are `@MainActor`, the `"a"` literal converts to `String?`. It is the same pattern as the neighbouring `everyWindowSeeingAChangeRunsItsReactionOnce`, with no new isolation crossing.

Nothing new added: no production code touched, no other test changed.

**Verified**
- Ran `swiftlint lint --strict` (0.65.1, the CI version and flags) on `MultiWindowTests.swift` and `AppLifecycle.swift`: exit 0, no violation. The file is 239 lines, its longest line 126 (limit 140).
- Read `AppLifecycle.swift`, `AppWideState.swift:15-19` and the whole test file at 264c45ca; 264c45ca is the worktree head.
- Not run: the app tests (no Xcode on Linux). The red-without-change claim and the compile check are by reading only; the macOS CI run is the arbiter.
